newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour closes gap on National in latest poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour closes gap on National in latest poll.

text.p: The main opposition centre- left Labour Party is just one point behind the conservative National Party in the latest NBR-Consultus opinion poll published on Friday.
National is the majority party in the coalition government.
The poll of 750 decided voters nationwide was conducted between Friday last week and Tuesday and has a margin of error of 3.5 percent.
It gives Labour 36 percent support, its highest level in this poll since May 1993 and well up on the 28 percent of the vote it won at the general election in October.
National was on 37 percent support, up three points on its election night vote.
National's coalition partner, New Zealand First, was down five points to eight percent support, compared with 13 percent on election night.
New Zealand First has lost support from voters who favoured a coalition with Labour and over the handling of a controversy over funding for Maori televison.
Support for the left-wing Alliance was at nine percent in the poll against 10 percent on election night.
Free-market Act New Zealand was also down one point on its election night support to five percent.
